school: 东汉女史学家、教育家与政治顾问：《汉书》十志以下八表与《天文志》的续成者，二十四史唯一的女主修者；曹世叔之妻，世称'曹大家'；和熹邓皇后临朝时的宫廷教师与政事顾问
historical_significance: 班昭（约49-约120），一名姬，字惠班，扶风安陵人，史学家班彪之女、《汉书》主修班固之妹、西域都护班超之妹；班固修《汉书》未竟而于公元92年因窦宪案牵连死于狱中，遗稿散乱，和帝下诏让班昭到东观藏书阁续成之——她补写八表（《百官公卿表》之外六表等）并续成《天文志》（一说由马续续成天文志而班昭整理定稿），使这部中国第一部纪传体断代史终成完帙；她常出入宫廷，为皇后与贵人们讲授经史，号'曹大家'；邓太后临朝后她参与政事顾问；她著《女诫》七章，是中国最早系统阐述女性规范的文章之一，亦作《东征赋》等辞赋；经学家马融曾从她受读《汉书》；她晚年为《汉书》作注（未竟）；约公元120年（一说117年）病逝，邓太后素服举哀以悼——她证明：'完成'本身就是一门手艺，一部巨著可以在两代人之间被一双手接稳并钉合，而学问与庙堂之门不必因性别而闭
historical_significance_en: Ban Zhao (c. 49 - c. 120), style name Huiban, of Fufeng Anling, was daughter of the historian Ban Biao, sister of Ban Gu, chief compiler of the 'Book of Han', and sister of Ban Chao, Protector General of the Western Regions. Ban Gu, his great history unfinished, was imprisoned in 92 on account of the Dou Xian affair and died there, his drafts in disorder; by imperial edict of Emperor He, Ban Zhao was summoned to the Eastern Lodge library to complete the work — she wrote the eight tables (six besides the Table of Officials) and finished the 'Treatise on Astronomy' (some say Ma Xu continued the astronomy treatise with her finalizing it), so that the first annals-biography dynastic history of China reached completeness. A frequent presence at court, she taught the classics to empresses and consorts and was honored as 'Cao Dagu' — Venerable Madame Cao, after her husband Cao Shishu. When Empress Dowager Deng took the regency she was consulted on affairs of state. Her 'Admonitions for Women' in seven chapters is one of China's earliest systematic treatises on female conduct; she also wrote the 'Rhapsody on the Eastern Journey'. The classicist Ma Rong received the 'Book of Han' from her teaching. In old age she annotated the 'Book of Han', unfinished at her death. She died c. 120 (some say 117), and Empress Dowager Deng wore mourning for her — proof that 'completion' is itself a craft, that a monumental history can be carried steady and riveted by one pair of hands across two generations, and that the gates of learning and of court need not close for sex.
unique_thinking: 班昭的独特处在于三重'接续者的主体性'：第一，她把'接手'做成'主修'——班固遗稿不是她替人誊抄的作业，而是她重新通读、辨明体例、补写缺卷的工程，八表与天文志在她的手中从残稿变成定本——她证明：接续不是复制原作者的意图，而是以同一部作品之名重新担起全部责任；第二，她把'宫廷女师'的身份做成学问与政治的通路——为皇后贵人讲经史不是消遣，而是把《汉书》的史学训练带进帝国最高决策层，邓太后临朝时的咨询使学术声望兑换成政治影响力——她证明：讲台可以是最深的一条参政通道；第三，她敢在同一只手里既立规范又被规范——'曹大家'以自身为范本立《女诫》，同时也以女主修者的实绩撑开了规范之外的缝隙——她证明：典范的力量在于它同时是约束与通行证
unique_thinking_en: Ban Zhao's singularity is a triple act of 'the successor's subjecthood'. First, she made 'taking over' into 'chief authorship': her brother's unfinished drafts were not a copyist's homework but a project she re-read whole, clarified in scheme, and completed with new books — the eight tables and the astronomy treatise became definitive in her hands — proof that succession is not the copying of another's intent but the shouldering, under the same title, of the whole responsibility. Second, she turned the standing of 'palace teacher' into a passage of learning into politics: teaching the classics to empresses was no pastime but the carrying of the historian's training of the 'Book of Han' into the empire's highest decisions; the consultations under Empress Dowager Deng converted scholarly standing into political force — proof that a lecture hall can be the deepest channel into statecraft. Third, she dared to be both rule-maker and rule-dweller in one hand: as 'Cao Dagu' she set 'Admonitions for Women' with herself as exemplar, while her very performance as the female compiler of a canonical history pried the door open beyond the rules — proof that an exemplar's power is that it is at once a constraint and a pass.
civilization_zh: 一世纪末至二世纪初的东汉洛阳——一位生于扶风班氏书香之家的女子，父亲班彪作《史记后传》，长兄班固承父业修《汉书》而瘐死狱中，次兄班超投笔从戎远镇西域；她在皇家藏书处东观藏书阁遍读典籍，接手兄长未竟的巨著，续写八表与《天文志》，成为二十四史中唯一的女主修者；她还是和熹邓皇后的老师，参与朝政顾问，以《女诫》七篇立闺训，七十岁高龄犹为《汉书》作注——她证明：一部断代史的完成，可以由一双手在两代人之间接续钉合，学问与权位都不因性别设限
civilization_en: Luoyang in the Eastern Han, from the late first into the early second century — a woman born into the scholarly Ban clan of Fufeng: her father Ban Biao wrote the 'Continuation of the Records'; her eldest brother Ban Gu carried on the 'Book of Han' and died in prison; her second brother Ban Chao threw down his brush for the sword and pacified the Western Regions. She read through the classics in the Eastern Lodge of the imperial library, took up her brother's unfinished masterwork, continued its eight tables and the 'Treatise on Astronomy', and stands as the only female chief compiler among the Twenty-Four Histories. She was also teacher to Empress Dowager Deng, consulted on state affairs, set seven chapters of 'Admonitions for Women', and in her seventies was still annotating the 'Book of Han' — proof that a dynastic history can be nailed together by one pair of hands across two generations, and that neither learning nor standing is fenced off by sex
key_works: 《汉书》八表与《天文志》（续成，约92-120年间）

cross_references.description_zh: 班昭与司马迁是'巨著的两种命运'的平行对：司马迁受了腐刑仍把《史记》独自写完——巨著由一人以受创之身扛到终点；班昭在兄长瘐死狱中、遗稿散乱之后受诏入东观——巨著由后继者以双倍的手接稳钉合——平行命题：一部巨著的完成不择手，可以是一人受难写尽，也可以是另一双手在死后十年接住；共同点是： whoever 接手，'完成'都要以主体身份而不是帮工身份来担。
cross_references.description_en: Ban Zhao and Sima Qian are a parallel pair of 'two fates of a masterwork': Sima Qian, punished by castration, carried the 'Records' alone to its end — a masterwork borne by one wounded body to the terminus; Ban Zhao, after her brother died in prison and his drafts scattered, was summoned into the Eastern Lodge — a masterwork steadied and riveted by a successor's doubled hands. The parallel thesis: a masterwork is indiscriminate about whose hands finish it — one wounded author may write it out alone, or another pair may catch it ten years after his death; what is shared is that whoever takes it up must bear 'completion' as a subject, not as a helper.

cross_references.description_zh: 班昭与李清照共享'女子接续文人未竟之业'的母题：李清照中年丧夫，独自整理《金石录》遗稿、作后序、表上于朝——把亡夫的收藏史钉成定本；班昭在兄长死后独自补《汉书》八表与天文志——把亡兄的断代史钉成定本——平行命题：未竟之作在女性手中不是负担而是署名机会：遗稿散乱处，正是署名者落笔处；两人都以整理定稿的动作把'妻子/妹妹'的身份升格为'作者'。
cross_references.description_en: Ban Zhao and Li Qingzhao share the motif of 'a woman completing a literatus's unfinished work': Li Qingzhao, widowed in midlife, alone collated the surviving drafts of the 'Jin Shi Lu', wrote its postface, and memorialized the finished book to the throne — nailing her late husband's history of collecting into its definitive form; Ban Zhao, after her brother's death, alone wrote the eight tables and the astronomy treatise of the 'Book of Han' — nailing her late brother's dynastic history into its definitive form. The parallel thesis: an unfinished work in a woman's hands is not a burden but a chance for signature — where the drafts scatter is precisely where the signer sets her brush; both raised the standing of 'wife/sister' into 'author' by the single act of seeing a text to its definitive form.

cross_references.description_zh: 班昭与吉布斯是'谁替你传播'的相反策略：吉布斯把划时代著作印成小册子寄给少数人然后沉默等世界发现——不设讲台；班昭则把东观当讲台，为皇后贵人面授经史，让声望经由学生（马融受读《汉书》、邓太后听政咨询）扩散——一个靠文本自己走路，一个靠讲授主动布道——对照命题：作品可以等人（吉布斯），也可以由讲台去追人（班昭）；对需要'被继承'的巨著而言，讲授往往比沉默更保险——没有班昭的讲席，《汉书》或许仍是一部残稿。
cross_references.description_en: Ban Zhao and Gibbs are opposite strategies of 'who spreads it for you': Gibbs printed his epochal work as a brochure for the few and fell silent to wait for the world to find it — no lecture hall; Ban Zhao made the Eastern Lodge a lectern, teaching the classics face to face to empresses and consorts, letting her standing travel through her students — Ma Rong receiving the 'Book of Han' from her, Empress Dowager Deng consulting her in the regency. One let the text walk by itself; the other preached actively from a podium. The contrast thesis: a work may wait for people (Gibbs) or be chased by the lectern (Ban Zhao); for a masterwork that needs to be inherited, teaching is the safer bet than silence — without Ban Zhao's chair, the 'Book of Han' might remain a heap of drafts.
